facts.fact: Techweez reports Kenya is migrating from NEMIS to the Kenya Education Management Information System (KEMIS), which became the required platform for the 2026 Grade 10 selection, with the PS telling the Public Accounts Committee that KEMIS is not yet complete.

Biometric Update reports Kenya will begin a pilot in July 2025 of the Kenya Education Management Information System (KEMIS) to replace NEMIS, set to fully go live by September, per Principal Secretary Julius Bitok.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Education KEMIS Secretariat circular says KEMIS holds learner records marked Valid or Invalid by an operational Learner Validation Engine and generates a Unique Learner Identifier (ULI) for learners in schools.

The circular says KEMIS compares learner records against KNEC examination and assessment databases and that parent or guardian identity details are needed for ULI creation and integration with national identity and civil registration records.

facts.fact: The Daily Nation reports that Kenya's government migrated in September 2025 from NEMIS to KEMIS, an integrated system designed to consolidate student records across the education sector from early childhood to tertiary.

facts.fact: KEMIS had captured about 5.057 million primary learners as at 10 November 2026 against 7.2 million expected, according to ministry official Mujumba Obwoyere.

The ministry allows learners without birth certificates to be captured on KEMIS using their parents' IDs, said Stephen Barongo, head of the Directorate of Primary Education; birth certificates were initially mandatory.

So They Can describes NEMIS as the Government's portal for data on education institutions, used to record school data and allocate school funding, with only 50% of enrolled primary children in its Baringo partner schools recorded.
